definition: An open scale-up interconnect standard from a consortium founded in 2024 (AMD, Intel, Google, Microsoft, Meta, AWS and others). It lets accelerators read and write each other's memory through UALink switches, using 200G lanes, in pods of up to 1,024 devices.

An Open Compute Project workstream, launched in 2025, that defines how to run scale-up traffic over Ethernet switches, including a compact header to cut overhead. It builds on Broadcom's Scale-Up Ethernet contribution.

Broadcom's framework, contributed to OCP in 2025, for using Ethernet switches such as Tomahawk Ultra as a scale-up fabric. It adds link-layer retry and credit-based flow control so short, lossless transfers work over Ethernet.

Carrying UALink's memory-style protocol across ordinary Ethernet switch chips instead of dedicated UALink switches. AMD's Helios rack uses it with Broadcom Tomahawk 6 switches while native UALink silicon is not yet available.

Communication in which one processor reads or writes another's memory directly with ordinary memory instructions, as NVLink allows, instead of packaging data into network messages. It cuts software overhead and latency for small, frequent transfers.
A mechanism that resends a corrupted frame between two directly connected ports instead of relying on end-to-end retransmission. It keeps scale-up links lossless with very low added latency.

A network in which each chip connects only to its neighbours along each dimension, with the ends wrapped around into rings. It scales to thousands of chips cheaply, but a message to a distant chip crosses many hops and shares bandwidth along the way.
Google's TPU-to-TPU links. Each chip has four or six ICI links to neighbouring chips, forming a 2D or 3D torus; Ironwood has six links at 200 GB/s each (bidirectional).
AWS's scale-up interconnect for Trainium chips. NeuronLink-v3 joins 64 Trainium2 in a torus; NeuronLink-v4 with NeuronSwitch-v1 joins 144 Trainium3 all-to-all at about 2 TB/s per chip.
Huawei's scale-up interconnect (also called Lingqu) used in CloudMatrix 384 and Atlas SuperPoDs. It links hundreds to thousands of Ascend NPUs through UB switches, largely over optics.

AMD's coherent interconnect family, used inside its chips and between MI300/MI350-series GPUs (as xGMI links) in a switchless eight-GPU mesh. AMD's 72-GPU Helios rack moves scale-up to UALink over Ethernet instead.

A chip that receives a weakened high-speed signal, recovers the data and retransmits it cleanly, extending how far a copper link can run. Common on PCIe and CXL links; Astera Labs is a leading supplier.

A small die, packaged next to a processor, that converts its electrical signals to light so data can leave the package on fibre. It promises scale-up links that span many racks at lower power than pluggable optics; Ayar Labs and Lightmatter build them.
